t:
(a) Army.—Section 3744 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in subsection (b)—
            (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “three years” and inserting “five years”; and 
            (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”; and  
        (2) in subsection (d)(1), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”.  
    (b) Air Force.—Section 8744 of such title is amended—
        (1) in subsection (b)—
            (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “three years” and inserting “five years”; and 
            (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”; and  
        (2) in subsection (d)(1), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”.

fable.w: This section only amends time periods in two title 10 provisions for the Army and Air Force, changing "three years" to "five years" and "two years" to "three years". There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 3744 of title 10, United States Code, is amended

opus.w: This section only lengthens time limits in sections 3744 and 8744 of title 10, which deal with Army and Air Force decorations. It does not require or allow any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory committee or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. Any link to 'recommendations' for awards comes from outside knowledge of the amended sections, not from this text, and those recommendations would stay within the military chain.
opus.s: in paragraph (1), by striking “three years” and inserting “five years”
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the amended sections of title 10 (sections 3744 and 8744, which set time limits for recommending and awarding Army and Air Force decorations) involve "recommendations," and so might seem procedural. That fails because this text only replaces time periods ("three years" becomes "five years," and "two years" becomes "three years"). It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue that involves anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory provisions regarding the length of service for Army and Air Force personnel. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or participation by non-federal entities. The changes are internal administrative adjustments to military service requirements.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Army.—Section 3744 of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) in subsection (b)— (A) in paragraph (1), by striking “three years” and inserting “five years”; and (B) in paragraph (2), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”; and (2) in subsection (d)(1), by striking “two years” and inserting “three years”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing service requirements could affect personnel decisions, but the text itself contains no mechanism for outside parties to participate in those decisions. It is purely an amendment to internal military regulations regarding service duration.
